items.informal_name: Weighted Homogeneity of Monomials in Multivariate Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] (w : σ → M)
  (d : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R) {m : M},
  (Finsupp.weight w) d = m → MvPolynomial.IsWeightedHomogeneous w ((MvPolynomial.monomial d) r) m
items.informal_description: For a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $, a monomial $ r \cdot X^d $ in the polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $, and a weight $ m \in M $, if the weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} d(i) \cdot w(i) = m $, then the monomial is weighted homogeneous of weight $ m $ with respect to $ w $.

items.informal_name: Weighted total degree of a multivariate polynomial
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {M : Type u_2} →
    [inst : CommSemiring R] →
      {σ : Type u_3} → [AddCommMonoid M] → [SemilatticeSup M] → (σ → M) → MvPolynomial σ R → WithBot M
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $, the weighted total degree of $ p $ is defined as the supremum of the weights of its monomials. Each monomial's weight is computed by summing the product of its exponent on each variable and the corresponding weight assigned by $ w $. The result is an element of $ \text{WithBot} \, M $, where $ \bot $ represents the case when $ p $ is the zero polynomial.

items.informal_name: Weighted total degree of a multivariate polynomial
items.type:

  {M : Type u_2} →
    [inst : CommSemiring R] →
      {σ : Type u_3} → [AddCommMonoid M] → [inst_2 : SemilatticeSup M] → [OrderBot M] → (σ → M) → MvPolynomial σ R → M
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and a weighting function $ w : \sigma \to M $ where $ M $ is a sup-semilattice, this function computes the supremum of the weights $ w(s) $ over all monomials $ s $ in the support of $ p $. The weight $ w(s) $ of a monomial $ s $ is defined as the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } s} s(i) \cdot v_i $ for some fixed vectors $ v_i $ associated with indices $ i $. The result is an element of $ M $ representing the weighted total degree of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order of a Monomial in Multivariate Power Series with Non-Zero Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {d : σ →₀ ℕ} {a : R},
  a ≠ 0 → MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w ((MvPowerSeries.monomial d) a) = ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, if $ f $ is a monomial $ \text{monomial}(d, a) $ where $ a \neq 0 $, then the weighted order of $ f $ with respect to a weight function $ w: \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $ is equal to the weighted sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $. In symbols, $ \text{weightedOrder}_w(\text{monomial}(d, a)) = \text{weight}_w(d) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order of a Monomial Equals Its Weight for Non-zero Coefficients
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {d : σ →₀ ℕ} {a : R} [inst_1 : Decidable (a = 0)],
  MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w ((MvPowerSeries.monomial d) a) = if a = 0 then ⊤ else ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, the weighted order of the monomial with coefficient $ a $ and exponent $ d $ is equal to the weight $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $ if $ a \neq 0 $, and $ \infty $ otherwise.
